title: Book One · Chapter 36: A Name on the Box
story:
Ronan writes his name on a strip of paper. The R is large. The last n is much smaller than the R.

He shows Mum. "I made this for my box."

"Which box?"

He points to the tea box by his bed.

"Good question," she says. "The kitchen box has towels in it now. You gave that one to me."

He pastes the strip below the blue flower. Inside are his three coins and the counting paper. He leaves the lid open until the paste dries.

The moving cart came through this gate several weeks ago. The tap is quiet. The old-house picture hangs above his bed. The pot has a small new leaf beside the three old ones. The leaf with the hole is still there.

Dad returned the old shop key. He looks for small repair jobs. People offer him small jobs. He takes those jobs. Some days he comes back with money. Other days, nobody has a job for him. He must ask again another day.

Mum has a little list of sewing jobs in her bag. She writes down each person's name herself. That list is for Mum's work. Ronan keeps his kite plans on his own paper.

On Monday afternoon, Leo comes to copy the test page. They want one copy each. The kite will stay by Ronan's door, high and dry, until they fly it together again.

Leo writes their names at the top of his page. He puts his own first.

Ronan notices. He almost says something. Then he looks at their first page. His own name is first on that page.

"Fair," he says.

Leo looks up. "What is?"

"Your name is first on your copy. Mine is first on this copy."

Leo grins and goes on copying.

They make a label for the string card. It says KITE STRING, NOT FOR CUTTING. Mum says the last part seems useful in this house. Dad says he can put the same words on his good work rope.

Mrs Lan comes to the back door carrying a small shirt. "A neighbour needs help with this pocket," Mrs Lan says. "Can you fix it?"

"Which neighbour?" Mum asks.

"The woman past the corner. Green door."

"There are two green doors," Ronan says.

Mrs Lan pauses. "You're right. The one beside the oil shop."

Mum writes the woman's name and the place on a fresh paper label. She pins it safely to the shirt. Ronan watches her put the pin in. She closes it under the cloth. The point is covered now.

Leo looks toward the gate.

"How many green doors are there on this street?"

"Three," Ronan says.

"Four. One at the far end."

"That one's blue."

"Blue-green."

They go to the gate with Mum's permission and look down the road. From here, the doors are patches of colour between people and hanging clothes.

"Let's draw the street," Leo says. "Then we can count the doors."

Ronan finds one of the clean paper scraps they kept. He draws a long line for the street. Leo puts a square at one end.

"Your gate."

"Not that end. School is that way."

They turn the paper. Now they are not sure. Is the gate at this end or that end?

Mum calls them back for water. The unfinished street lies on the table beside the drying label. Ronan sees his name clearly on the tea box. The tea box is his. His name is on it. He looks back at the little squares. Which one is their gate? Which is the school? He and Leo need to look at the real street again.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：label＝标签；copy＝抄写；gate＝院门；pins＝用别针固定。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 给哪些东西做了标签？
2. 这一章结尾出现了什么新问题？
